decision.scope: exact extracted-frame SHA-256 memoization within one analysis run only
basis: Screen fixture: 6→4 Tesseract calls, OCR wall -33.0%, analyzer wall -24.7%.
Dense duplicate fixture: 21→5 Tesseract calls, OCR wall -74.8%, analyzer wall -48.4%.
Sparse all-distinct control: 2→2 calls, analyzer wall -0.2%; no material regression.
Authorized real all-distinct control: 8→8 calls, analyzer wall -3.6%; no material regression.
All evidence and semantic-input files were byte-equivalent within each A/B pair.

uncertainty: Each cell is one run; timing deltas are observed comparisons rather than a stable performance distribution.
The large benefit is specific to exact duplicate extracted bytes; no benefit is claimed for visually similar but non-identical frames.
The real control produced no cache hits, so its timing difference reflects ordinary run variance rather than memoization savings.
Raw private video remained local and is represented in GitHub only by its content hash and measurements.
conclusion: P-002 passes all predeclared correctness and performance gates. Adopt exact-frame-SHA memoization for a separately reviewed integration, while keeping the current production/default path unchanged in this experiment.
